newsitem.title: USA: Worldwide chip sales rose 4.9 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide chip sales rose 4.9 pct in March.

text.p: Worldwide chip sales rose 4.9 percent in March over February levels, the Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) reported Monday.
SIA said worldwide chip sales in March totaled $10.91 billion, up from $10.4 billion in February.
However, sales were down 9.9 percent from March of 1996, when chip sales totaled $12.1 billion.

Compared with February of this year, chip sales in March were up in all major markets, SIA said. Sales in the Americas market, encompassing North and South America, rose 7.3 percent to $3.67 billion. In the Asia Pacific region, sales rose 6.8 percent to $2.31 billion. Sales in Europe rose 4.8 percent to $2.35 billion, and sales in Japan rose 0.2 percent to $2.58 billion.
SIA said sales in Japan were impacted by the declining value of the yen, which has fallen about 10 percent since December.

The largest drop in sales from last March came from the Japanese market, where sales fell 14.5 percent. March-to March chip sales were down 9.8 percent in both the Americas and in Europe and fell 4.2 percent in the Asia Pacific region.
March sales figures were compiled by the 70-member World Semiconductor Trade Statistics organization.
